intro: Seattle listings advertise 10x10 units from about $32, while typical non-climate 10x10 street rates run about $185–$188/month. Once the move-in special ends and the first existing-customer increase lands, your six-month average is well above the number on the banner.

units.notes: Locker / closet size. Fixed fees dominate the true cost at this size. Climate-controlled ~$70–$73.
Walk-in closet; studio overflow. No reliable lowest-promo figure published for this size (gap). Climate-controlled ~$118–$125.
Most rented size. City average $185 (StorageCafe, Sep 2026); Seattle–Tacoma metro averages $170 (Storage Stats), down 13.4% YoY — strong leverage when negotiating. Climate-controlled ~$177–$235.
Two-bedroom contents. Estimate: single source (StorageCafe, Sep 2026). Climate-controlled ~$241–$252.
Three-bedroom home or a car. Climate-controlled ~$301–$308.

local_tips: Seattle asking rents are falling fast (down about 13% YoY across the metro per Storage Stats), so quote the current new-customer rate when an increase notice arrives.
Climate-controlled units in Seattle can cost about the same as, or less than, standard units (StorageCafe) — compare both.
Cheapest areas per StorageCafe include Riverview (~$72) and Olympic Hills (~$115); Mount Baker and the Central Waterfront are the most expensive (~$276–$281).
Rates tend to be lowest around February and highest in August (StorageCafe).
